newsitem.title: TURKEY: POLITICAL FEARS KEEP TURKISH BOND YIELDS FIRMER.
newsitem.headline: POLITICAL FEARS KEEP TURKISH BOND YIELDS FIRMER.

text.p: Turkish bond yields jumped more than five points in two days amid concerns over the fate of Islamist-led coalition government and bankers said the upward trend would continue unless uncertainties are eliminated.
Bond yields have risen around five points in papers with 1998 maturities.

"There is a rising uncertainty in the markets over the fate of coalition government and that raised bond yields. The worst thing is uncertainty. The upward trend may continue in that case," said Ali Ozenc, money market manager at private bank Finansbank.
Turkish markets opened uneasy on Thursday due to mounting political uncertainties after a 6-1/5 day holiday.
The most active April 22, 1998 paper yields rose to 99.27 percent on Friday, up two points from Thursday's 97.06.
Ozenc said the collapse of the government or the establishment of a new one would not distort the financial stability but the worst thing would be an early election or a military rule.

"Bond rates have reached their peak, reflecting the recent political developments. For a further rise, there must be a possibility of early elections this year," said another private bank treasury manager.

Bond yields had surged to 105-110 percent levels in early March, amid higher-than expected inflation figures and increased political tension following the National Security Council's (NSC) warnings on February 28. They later stabilised at between 90-94 percent levels.

Bankers said the market was awaiting Saturday's NSC meeting amid rifts between the coalition government's Islamist and conservative wings following the secularist military's demands to combat rising Islamist activism.
"The outcome of the NSC meeting is very important. If negative news comes out the meeting, bond yields may go up," Ozenc said.
The military members of the NSC are expected to increase demands on the reluctant government to implement anti-Islamist measures put forward by the generals at a February meeting.

Daily Yeni Yuzyil on Friday quoted unnamed cabinet ministers as saying Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller had decided to pull her conservative True Path Party (DYP) out of the 10-month-old Islamist-led coalition.
Bankers said political developments would dominate the market in the coming days.
They say the impact of economic events will remain minor as they do not expect any jump in inflation in coming months when foreign currency inflow increases because of tourism earnings.
The treasury will not hold any bond auction by the end of this month due to its favourable cash flow.
Treasury officials say lessened debt servicing and increased tax collection will help the treasury rely less on domestic borrowing in coming months.
Bankers believe this would ease pressures on bond rates. --Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 08 75
